mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in workplace attendance, evidenced by two consecutive weeks of significant increases, signals a return of commuting routines that will lift weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES showing two consecutive weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: As transit station activity continues its recent upward trend and crosses a critical threshold, it indicates sufficient public movement and confidence to support a rebound in discretionary retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show an increase compared to the last 14 days, even if TRANSIT rises above -15% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent trend of people spending less time at home and more time at workplaces signifies a broader shift in daily routines, directly translating to increased engagement in retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL decreasing and WORKPLACES increasing over the period.

mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC, following a dip, suggests that the sector has bottomed out and is entering a recovery phase, driven by easing restrictions or increased consumer confidence, leading to further gains over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC shows week-on-week improvement for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show a sustained increase, or its mean is lower than the last 28 days, even if it showed a week-on-week improvement at the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in parks visitation, combined with already negative retail and recreation mobility, indicates a general decrease in discretionary outdoor and leisure activities, leading to further stagnation or decline in retail over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -10% for two consecutive weeks AND RETAIL_REC remains below -5%
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 14 days, despite PARKS remaining below -10% and RETAIL_REC remaining below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently high grocery and pharmacy visits establish a stable baseline of essential community movement, which, when combined with other positive indicators, provides a foundation for discretionary retail to recover over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 10% for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, even with GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 10% for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp and concurrent week-on-week rebound in both workplace and transit mobility over the last two weeks indicates a strong immediate return to out-of-home activities, which will directly boost retail and recreation footfall in the very short term (next week).
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week (t+1w) does not show an increase compared to t-0w, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT showing two consecutive weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in residential mobility over the past two weeks signals a fundamental shift in daily patterns, with people spending less time at home and more time engaging in out-of-home activities, which will broadly support an increase in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL shows a decreasing trend for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL showing a consistent decreasing trend for at least two consecutive weeks.
